objectives.title: Read the flag
objectives.prompt: Spray a short list of common candidate passwords across the domain user roster, find the single account that authenticates (the one reusing the weak onboarding default), then read flag.txt from the //dc/storeops share that only that account may open.
hints: No credentials are handed out, but the user roster is known (and enumerable over null/low-priv LDAP on 389). Account lockout is disabled, so you can safely try one password against every user.

Spray a short list of common candidates (onboarding default / season + year, capitalised, with digits: Spring2024, Summer2024, Autumn2024, Winter2023, ...) across the roster: nxc smb <dc> -u users.txt -p 'Summer2024' --continue-on-success, or kerbrute passwordspray. Exactly one account comes back positive.
The hit is k.verma / Summer2024. Read the flag with it: smbclient //dc/storeops -U 'SUMMIT\k.verma%Summer2024' -c 'get flag.txt'.

steps.title: Name the technique
steps.prompt: What is the name of the attack that tries one (or a few) common passwords against many accounts to stay under lockout thresholds?

steps.title: Name the misconfiguration
steps.prompt: Which account policy setting, when disabled or set too high, makes spraying safe for an attacker? (two words)

steps.title: Find the sprayable account
steps.prompt: Which account authenticates with a sprayed password? (username)

steps.title: Recover the password
steps.prompt: Which default password does that account reuse?

steps.title: Name the loot share
steps.prompt: Which SMB share holds the flag, readable only by the sprayed-in account?
